abort.no_devices_found: No Boks found. Make sure a Bluetooth adapter or an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy is in range, and that the official dongle is unplugged (it holds the connection).

init.title: Link settings
init.description: Saving reloads the link without restarting Home Assistant. Note: the integration's Python code is not reloaded — after updating the component files, a restart is still required.

data_description.label: For example F540 — the reference printed on your mailbox or shown in your account. The Boks does not expose it over Bluetooth (its Serial Number characteristic returns its own MAC address), so it has to be typed in. The device will then be named “Boks F540”: essential as soon as you manage several mailboxes, which would otherwise all carry the same name.
data_description.keepalive: The Boks closes the connection after about 30 s of silence. A longer interval means fewer exchanges (and lower power draw) while the link is held, but moves closer to that cutoff: beyond it the link drops and reconnects in a loop, which costs more.
data_description.reconnect_max: Ceiling for the delay, which doubles on every failure. A high value spares the batteries while the Boks is out of range; a low one shortens the time to come back online.
data_description.open_code_mode: Choose how to open the mailbox from Home Assistant, or leave “No code” to stay strictly read-only. Depending on the choice, a second screen asks for the code, the secrets.yaml reference, or a list of one-time codes.
data_description.config_key: 8 hexadecimal characters (your mailbox's Config Key, retrievable from your account), or a secrets.yaml reference: !secret boks_config_key. Filling this in enables the ADMIN functions: enrol/revoke a Mifare badge and toggle VIGIK. This is a more powerful secret than the open code — anyone with access to Home Assistant could then enrol their own badge. Leaving it empty exposes none of these functions.
data_description.refresh_interval: Every N minutes, history (last VIGIK / code openings) is re-read — whether the link is held (re-requested within the same session, since otherwise history is only read once at connect) or not (a dedicated short connection). Goal: mirror the official BoksLINK dongle's continuous monitoring, but reporting to Home Assistant instead of the Boks cloud. 0 disables it. WARNING: reading history DRAINS the box log (persistent cursor, which serves as the offline backlog for the official dongle) — regular draining may cause openings to be lost from the official cloud history if it comes back online. An explicit choice.

open_code.title: Open code
open_code.description: Mode chosen: {mode}. Leaving this field empty keeps the integration read-only.

data_description.open_code_value: Depending on the mode chosen on the previous screen: the code itself (6 characters over the alphabet 0123456789AB) for “Permanent code”; the key name in secrets.yaml (without the !secret prefix) for “secrets.yaml reference”; a list of one-time codes, one per line, for “OTP codes” — each code is only removed from the pool once the mailbox has actually used it, never before. Whatever the mode, filling this in adds an Open button: anyone with access to Home Assistant will then be able to open the mailbox.

error.invalid_open_code: Invalid code: 6 characters, only 0-9, A and B (one per line in OTP mode).
error.invalid_config_key: Invalid Config Key: exactly 8 hexadecimal characters (0-9, A-F).
error.unknown_secret: That key was not found in secrets.yaml (or holds no text).
error.no_codes_entered: Enter at least one code, one per line.
